purpose: Single Source of Truth (SSOT) for CYNIC canonical vocabulary. Eliminates jargon drift, homonyms, and palimpsest naming.

DeploymentTier.definition: Lifecycle environment stage for deployment and validation.
DeploymentTier.rationale: An environment tier is not a test harness. A harness is a test execution apparatus, never a target deployment stage.

TestHarness.definition: Execution scaffold and evaluation instrumentation for measuring agents, benchmarks, models, or regression suites.
banned_usages: Using harness to describe production or staging environments

Authority.definition: The legitimate, verifiable constituent or delegated source of decision power.
banned_usages: Arbitrary enum levels masquerading as authority gates without signed receipts

Grant.definition: A bounded, non-transferable, time-leased and workload-specific delegation of authority.

Service.definition: A bounded sovereign system daemon, process, or LXC compute unit with health signals.
banned_usages: Vague synonym for pure Rust domain modules

MonotonicRatchet.definition: A compliance and health assertion enforcing that measured debt never increases (current <= ceiling) while allowing debt reduction without breaking the gate.
MonotonicRatchet.prescribed_usage: All governance checks measuring retired metaphors, god-object size limits, and transitional debt.
banned_usages: Using strict scalar equality (actual == declared) that penalizes debt payoff or unblocks only with synchronous manual contract updates

TopologyGenerator.definition: Pure inference engine that derives the workspace directed acyclic graph (DAG) and canonical extraction order directly from Cargo metadata and layer rules.
TopologyGenerator.prescribed_usage: Always derived via cynic audit topology --apply, never manually authored in infra/crate-topology.json.
banned_usages: Feature-gating the topology generator behind obscure or uncompiled build flags
Hand-editing topological dependency edges or extraction order

PassiveFixture.definition: Non-executable evaluation data, historical traces, session snapshots, or training labels stored for test verification.
banned_usages: Treating captured test traces or eval datasets as active executable workspace path consumers

ArtifactPublicationTransport.definition: Typed network protocol (TransportProtocol enum) governing binary artifact release and node deployment.
banned_usages: Passing raw string literals for publication transport protocols in domain code and tests

NodeRole.definition: Canonical top-level topological role of a node in the CYNIC mesh. Follows the agnostic distributed systems standard with 5 invariant roles: compute, storage, gateway, control, workstation. Specializations are expressed via capability flags, not hardcoded software roles.
banned_usages: Passing software-coupled or metaphor-based role names (cortex_host, mesh_coordinator, forge_primary, storage_primary) as canonical NodeRole values

BuildAction.definition: Canonical lifecycle action for a build workload execution on the builder pool.
banned_usages: Using arbitrary string verbs for build workload actions

BuildRole.definition: Canonical execution role of a node capable of running build workloads.
banned_usages: Using hardcoded node IPs or software-coupled names for build runners

EvidenceKind.definition: Canonical discriminator for captured machine receipts and evidence envelopes.
banned_usages: Substring matching against arbitrary string identifiers to classify evidence

ArtifactTransport.definition: Sovereign protocol and payload abstraction governing binary artifact transfer, staging, and publication.
banned_usages: Maintaining separate, drifted HTTP transport mechanisms for runtime staging versus release publication

RefactorCollisionRisk.definition: Assessed collision risk of a refactor or absorption candidate against in-flight work, derived from observable churn, test coverage, modularity, active-refactor overlap, and churning dependencies.
RefactorCollisionRisk.rationale: A risk level is an assessment, not a deployment tier or a test harness. Canonicalized so the heuristic (cynic-audit-engine/refactor_risk) and the CynicErrorCode (ArchitectureRefactorCollisionRisk) share one vocabulary.

Fleet.definition: The set of enrolled CYNIC mesh nodes (fleet mesh) operating under a shared membership and topology authority.
Fleet.rationale: Fleet designates the enrolled node set; FleetMesh conflates the set with the mesh transport (Headscale/WireGuard) that connects it.
banned_usages: Using FleetMesh for the node set itself rather than the mesh transport

MeshNode.definition: A member node of the fleet mesh, identified by id/name/IP, with online status and last-seen observation (cynic-types fleet_mesh port).
MeshNode.rationale: MeshNode is the canonical pure port type in cynic-types; FleetNetworkNode (cynic-network), MeshMember (mesh_coordination ports) and FleetNode* observation wrappers are ad-hoc surface names for the same member.
banned_usages: Defining parallel node-member types outside the cynic-types fleet_mesh port

BuildRunner.definition: Port executing build commands on a build-capable node (cynic-build ports trait, run_command via argv).
BuildRunner.rationale: BuildRunner is the canonical hexagonal port; RemoteRunner is the ad-hoc enrollment-surface name for a remotely enrolled build runner.
banned_usages: Using RemoteRunner as a synonym for the BuildRunner port

Claim.definition: Hierarchical coordination claim over a scope (fleet, node, crate, module, file) with type, status, budget and TTL (cynic-protocol agent_coordination).
Claim.rationale: Claim is the canonical protocol type; WorkloadClaim is the ad-hoc scheduler-surface renaming of the same claim.
banned_usages: Using WorkloadClaim for a protocol Claim

Budget.definition: Bounded resource allowance (energy/time/steps) attached to an agent claim or capability lease request.
Budget.rationale: Budget is the canonical concept name; AgentBudgets is the ad-hoc agent-surface struct name (cynic-protocol agent_citizenship) for the same allowance.
banned_usages: Using AgentBudgets as the canonical budget vocabulary

Lease.definition: Time-bounded, scope- and budget-bounded capability delegation (LeaseRequest -> CapabilityLease -> LeaseReceipt, cynic-protocol capability_lease).
Lease.rationale: Lease is the canonical delegation concept; DeliveryLease (agent workload delivery surface) and LeaseGrant (storage/coordination surfaces) are ad-hoc surface renamings.
banned_usages: Using DeliveryLease or LeaseGrant as generic lease vocabulary

Session.definition: Bounded interactive or execution session with its own store, metadata and lifecycle (chat, inference and supervisor sessions).
Session.rationale: Session is the canonical concept; ChatSession (chat surface) and SessionStore (store surface) are ad-hoc surface names for session state.
banned_usages: Using ChatSession or SessionStore as canonical session vocabulary

EvidenceEnvelope.definition: Content-addressed, provenance-bearing evidence container with schema, digest, subject, producer and payload (cynic-protocol evidence, cynic.evidence.envelope.v1).
EvidenceEnvelope.rationale: EvidenceEnvelope is the canonical wire type; EvidenceRef and EvidenceStore are ad-hoc surface names conflating a reference or a persistence port with the envelope itself.
banned_usages: Using EvidenceRef or EvidenceStore for the evidence envelope wire type

NodeIdentity.definition: Full cryptographic identity of a CYNIC node: ed25519 signing key plus 128-bit NodeId fingerprint derived via BLAKE3 (cynic-secrets types).
NodeIdentity.rationale: NodeIdentity is the canonical full identity; MachineIdentity is the ad-hoc surface synonym and NodeId alone names only the fingerprint, not the full identity.
banned_usages: Using MachineIdentity for NodeIdentity, or NodeId for the full cryptographic identity

Capability.definition: Exhaustive federation capability a node may be granted, decided by the single role-to-capability table (cynic-protocol federation_authz).
Capability.rationale: Capability is the canonical exhaustive enum; EngineCapability is the ad-hoc engine-surface renaming of the same grantable capability.
banned_usages: Using EngineCapability for federation Capability
